title: int3 converter deployment caused stability regressions and subtle accuracy divergence
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: After rolling out a converter change (bitpack-v2) that enables 3-bit weight packing for int3 profiles, we observed two failure modes across hosted and dedicated serving: (1) crashloops / segfaults on specific GPU kernel paths for models using fused attention, and (2) silent accuracy divergence for a small set of RLHF models (higher token-level hallucination on evaluation prompts). The change was rolled back to stop new regressions. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and longer-term guards to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2025-02-10: Deploy bitpack-v2 converter into canary pipeline
2025-02-10 11:45 UTC: First crashloop observed on dedicated pool dc-eu-1 for model 'redwood-rlhf-v2-int3-canary'
2025-02-10 12:10 UTC: Streaming errors spike and fallback rate to fp16 increases; SRE throttles traffic to canary
2025-02-10 13:00 UTC: Host L1 rollback of converter change to bitpack-v1 (stop gap)
2025-02-11: Engineers reproduce crash locally using patched packer with address sanitizer; find alignment/stride mismatch for grouped quant blocks
2025-02-12: Eval team reports 0.9% accuracy drop on curated RLHF prompt set for converted int3 models compared to pre-change baseline
2025-02-14: Hotfix PR to add stricter preflight validation merged to main and cherry-picked to runtime-1.26
2025-02-18: Canary with additional telemetry rolled out; no new crashes but accuracy monitoring still shows drift for subset of model configs
root_cause: Multiple interacting issues: (1) Converter change introduced a new packing ordering for grouped 3-bit blocks (bitpack-v2). The ordering mismatch caused some kernels to interpret scales and zero-points in the wrong permutation leading to numerical differences and, on certain fused kernels, memory mis-alignment that triggered occasional segfaults. (2) Our preflight checks only ran parity against a small set of ops and did not exercise fused-attention kernels or long-sequence generation traces, so the accuracy regression was not caught before rollout. (3) Telemetry lacked op-fallback and per-op precision histograms; when fallback to fp16 happened for a subset, it masked upstream divergences until customers saw quality issues.
impact_summary:
- Internal canary traffic: ~1200 requests/min over 2h that hit the bad converter
- Dedicated pool impact: 6 instances entered crashloop, causing degraded capacity for one customer-managed deployment (1 customer saw increased latency and some 5xxs)
- Hosted API: increased op-fallback rate (int3->fp16) in ~0.6% of requests for the affected model family; observable quality drift on 3 RLHF models used in our eval suite
- No customer data loss; no secret leakage. Business impact limited by quick rollback and throttling, but this is high priority due to P0 customer SLA sensitivity
actions_taken:
1) Rolled back converter to bitpack-v1 on 2025-02-10 to stop immediate crashes.
2) Throttled canary traffic and isolated affected dedicated pool nodes.
3) Emergency test harness created to reproduce crash with ASAN and run long-sequence generation (link below).
4) Hotfix preflight validation merged adding: per-op golden outputs, fused-kernel exercise, and packing-order checksum.
5) Canary re-deployed on 2025-02-18 with enhanced telemetry and staged ramp
action_items: AI-1: Implement a packing-order compatibility validator in the converter: fail conversion if packing checksum != expected format (owner: Diego; due: 2025-02-20)
AI-2: Add op-level deterministic golden-output tests for fused-attention and KV-cache warmup sequences in the model conversion CI (owner: Priya Singh; due: 2025-02-25)
AI-3: Instrument per-op precision and fallback metrics in runtime to alert when fallback rate > 0.1% for any model-version (owner: SRE team - Alex Chen; due: 2025-02-21)
AI-4: Expand converter canary to include RLHF eval suite with full-generation traces and log token-level diff stats (owner: Eval - Tomas Ortega; due: 2025-02-26)
AI-5: Kernel alignment sanity checks in serving runtime to reject misaligned packed buffers rather than allow kernel to proceed and crash (owner: Runtime - Lila Park; due: 2025-03-05)

AI-6: Postmortem follow-up: schedule cross-team runbook review (Runtime, Converter, Canary, Eval) and update rollout checklist to require end-to-end eval for new packing formats (owner: Maya Thompson; due: 2025-03-03)
AI-7: Backfill historical telemetry for last 90 days to surface latent accuracy drift signals that may correlate with previous converter updates (owner: Observability - Noor Patel; due: 2025-03-10)
AI-8: Add model conversion compatibility matrix to internal docs and gate conversions for model families known to use fused kernels heavily (owner: Product - Aaron Blake; due: 2025-03-01)
AI-9: Create a canary signal in Console to show per-route quantization health (fallbacks, op errors, accuracy regressions) for customer-facing transparency (owner: Console - Mei Lin; due: 2025-03-15)
AI-10: Run a week-long stability burn of int3 canary on dedicated pools with real traffic mirror before any future converter format changes (owner: SRE/Release - Diego Alvarez; due: 2025-03-12)
followups:
- Weekly sync established: Tuesdays 15:00 UTC with Runtime, Converter, Eval, SRE, and Observability until all AI items are done.
- Track progress via project board quant-infra-stability and mark tickets as dependent.
- Plan for a broader 'format transition' working group to define and version converter formats (semver + migration tests).
notes: Engineering decisions: we prefer a conservative conversion compatibility model (reject unknown packing variants) rather than runtime heuristics that guess packing at serve-time. This reduces surface area for subtle numerical divergence. The team agreed to treat new packing formats as major-versioned features with mandatory end-to-end eval before rollout.
